mainTopic: A חטאת must belong to its owner and match its exact sin, yet in the קרבן עולה ויורד set-aside money may move between levels as the owner's wealth changes.
overview: The amud has two משניות. The first teaches that a חטאת is tied to its owner and to its exact sin. If the owner dies, his son may not bring it. The owner himself may not move it to another sin, even from one eating of חלב to another. A long ברייתא learns this step by step from 'קרבנו' (his own offering) and 'על חטאתו' (for that very sin): no father's animal, no father's money, no switching one's own animal, and no switching one's own money. רב שמואל בר שימי explains why money needed its own teaching: switched money can lose its holiness through מעילה, so one might think switching is allowed from the start. The second משנה teaches that in the קרבן עולה ויורד, set-aside money follows the owner's wealth, going down from lamb to bird to עשירית האיפה, or back up. The גמרא shows that the phrases ״מחטאתו״ and ״על חטאתו״ are each needed, because flour is not a blood offering. The amud ends as רבי אלעזר begins a case of a rich מטמא מקדש who set aside birds, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: a designated sin offering cannot be transferred
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a son may not bring his dead father's designated חטאת. It also rules that a person may not move his own חטאת from one sin to another, even between two sins of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person sets aside a חטאת and then dies, his son may not bring it in his place. A person also may not take a חטאת set aside for one sin and bring it for a different sin. Even if he set it aside for חלב he ate yesterday, he may not bring it for חלב he ate today. The פסוק says 'his offering for his sin': the offering must be brought for the exact sin it was set aside for.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two rules: a son cannot use his father's חטאת, and a חטאת cannot be switched from one sin to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second rule goes surprisingly far. Even two sins of the exact same type (eating חלב twice) count as different sins, so an animal set aside for one cannot cover the other. The source is the phrase 'קרבנו על חטאתו': the offering is tied to one specific sin.

steps.title: Where does the son rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that a son cannot bring his father's חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the משנה's rule. This sets up the ברייתא that answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brought a פסוק only for the rule about switching sins. The גמרא now wants a source for the first rule, that a son cannot use his father's offering.

steps.title: The word 'his offering' excludes the father's offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'קרבנו' (his offering) that a person fulfills his obligation only with his own offering, not his father's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'His offering.' With his own offering he fulfills his obligation, but not with his father's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the word 'קרבנו' as meaning 'his own offering.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra 'his' in 'his offering' limits the offering to its owner. An animal the father set aside is the father's offering, so the son cannot use it.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "His offering" –

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'קרבנו' teaches that only one's own offering counts, so a father's offering does not.

steps.title: Maybe the rule applies only when the two sins differ in severity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the rule might be narrow. Perhaps the son is blocked only when his sin and his father's sin differ in severity. When they are equal, perhaps he may use the father's animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the son fails to fulfill his obligation with his father's animal only when it goes from a lighter sin to a more serious one, or from a more serious one to a lighter one. But perhaps he does fulfill it with the father's offering when it goes from light to light, or from serious to serious?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible limit on the rule it just taught. This sets up the next answer from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning behind this 'you might think': if the sins don't match, the animal plainly does not fit. If they match, maybe the father's animal is a fair substitute. The ברייתא raises this so it can rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think' – a possible but wrong idea that the ברייתא then rules out
A lighter, less serious sin
A more serious sin

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on using a father's offering apply even when the father's sin and the son's sin are equally severe?

steps.title: A second 'his offering' rules out even equal sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק: 'קרבנו' again teaches that the son cannot use his father's offering, even when the two sins are equally severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'His offering.' With his own offering he fulfills his obligation, but not with his father's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 4. It brings 'קרבנו' again, this time to show the rule has no exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is ownership, not whether the sins match. Even when the sins are equal, the animal still belongs to the father, so it is not the son's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches' – introduces a proof from a verse

phrases.english: The verse states: "His offering" –

phrases.english: with his own offering he fulfills his obligation,
but he does not fulfill it with his father's offering.

steps.whatToRemember: A son can never use the animal his father set aside as a חטאת, even if the son's sin is just as severe as his father's.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow reading raised in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated 'קרבנו' shows that even between equally severe sins, the son cannot use his father's offering.

steps.title: A new 'you might think' compares the case to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now accepts that the father's animal itself can never be used. It supports this with the rule of a נזיר, who cannot finish his נזירות with an animal his father set aside. This line sets up a further question, which step 7 finishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he does not fulfill his obligation with an animal his father set aside, even from light to light or serious to serious, since a person cannot shave at the end of his נזירות with an animal his father set aside...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a new 'you might think.' It agrees the father's animal is unusable and brings the case of a נזיר as a parallel. The sentence is not finished yet; it is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here the ברייתא proved that the father's animal cannot be used. Now it takes that as settled and compares it to a נזיר, who also cannot bring his closing offerings from an animal his father set aside. The rest of this new idea comes in the next part of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: For behold; since – brings a supporting reason
Shaves; here, completing נזירות by shaving and bringing the closing offerings
The vow of a נזיר

phrases.english: One might think he does not fulfill his obligation with his father's offering
with an animal that he designated,
even from a lighter sin to a lighter one,
or from a more serious sin to a more serious one,
since one does not shave at the end of his naziriteship
with an animal that his father designated,

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as going back on step 5. The ברייתא agrees the father's animal cannot be used. It is preparing a new question that comes next.
steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יֵצֵא בְּקׇרְבַּן אָבִיו בִּבְהֵמָה שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ אֲפִילּוּ

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Building on the rule that the father's animal is unusable and the parallel to נזיר, the ברייתא is setting up a further question, which step 7 completes.

steps.title: Perhaps the son can use his father's money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that even if the father's animal is off-limits, the son could still use money the father set aside, because a נזיר can use his father's unallocated money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he can fulfill his obligation with money his father set aside, even from a lighter sin for a more serious one, or from a more serious sin for a lighter one. After all, a person can bring the offerings at the end of his נזירות with money his father set aside, as long as the money was not yet assigned to specific offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the question that began in the last step. The animal is ruled out, but maybe money is different, as it is with a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is more flexible than an animal because it has not yet become a specific קרבן. The ברייתא brings support from נזיר: a son may use his father's money set aside for נזירות if it is סתומים, meaning not yet earmarked for a particular offering. So maybe the son can also use the father's money for his own חטאת, even when the sins differ in severity.

steps.title: קרבנו rules out even the father's money
steps.stepSummary: The word ׳קרבנו׳ teaches that a person fulfills his obligation only with his own offering, so even the father's money cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ׳his offering׳: he fulfills his obligation with his own offering, not with his father's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the same word ׳קרבנו׳. It blocks the father's money too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to נזיר does not carry over to חטאת. ׳קרבנו׳ requires the חטאת to be his own, so anything the father set aside for his own חטאת is excluded, whether it is an animal or money.

keyTerms.meaning: He fulfills his obligation with his own offering

steps.title: Perhaps his own animal can be switched between sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now suggests the opposite side: the father's money is fully excluded, but a person's own animal could be used for a different sin of his, even one of different severity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he cannot use money his father set aside, even between sins of equal severity. But he can use an offering he set aside for himself, even from a severe sin for a lenient one or from a lenient sin for a severe one?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא accepts that the father's money is off-limits. It now asks about an animal the person set aside for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ׳קרבנו׳ only stresses that the offering must be his own, maybe anything that is his own works. So an animal he set aside for one sin could be used for a different sin of his, whatever the severity.

steps.title: The offering must be for its own sin
steps.stepSummary: The words ׳קרבנו על חטאתו׳ teach that the offering must be brought for the specific sin it was set aside for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ׳his offering for his sin׳: it works only when it is brought for the sake of that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea of switching one's own animal to a different sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added words ׳על חטאתו׳ show that being his own is not enough. The animal is tied to the sin it was set aside for, so moving it to another sin does not work.

steps.title: Perhaps his own money can be switched freely
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that a person's own animal can never be switched, even between equal sins, but money he set aside for himself may be used for any of his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he cannot use an animal he set aside for himself for another sin, even between equal sins. For if he set aside an animal for eating חלב and brought it for eating דם, or set it aside for דם and brought it for חלב, he has not committed מעילה and has not gained atonement. But maybe he can use money he set aside for himself, between equal sins or between sins of different severity?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא accepts that his own animal is locked to its sin. Now it asks whether his own money is more flexible. Step 12 gives the reason for this idea, and step 13 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of חלב and דם shows that an animal cannot move even between equal sins, since bringing it for the wrong sin gives no atonement. Money, though, has not yet become a specific animal, so maybe it can be used for any of his sins. Step 13 answers this new question.

steps.title: Why money might be switchable between sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the reason for its suggestion. If someone uses his own חטאת money for a different sin, he has committed מעילה, and the offering still atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is why we might think so: if he set aside money for himself for the sin of eating חלב and used it for the sin of eating דם, or set it aside for דם and used it for חלב, he has committed מעילה and the offering atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the suggestion from step 11 by giving its reason. Money used for the wrong sin counts as מעילה, yet the offering bought with it still atones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals and money are treated differently here. Misusing consecrated money takes away its holiness, so after the switch the money is like ordinary money and the offering works. Based on that, one might think switching money between sins is allowed from the start.

steps.title: The פסוק requires the offering to be for its own specific sin
steps.stepSummary: The words ׳קרבנו על חטאתו׳ teach that even money must be used only for the sin it was set aside for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ׳קרבנו על חטאתו׳, his offering for his sin. He does not fulfill his obligation until his offering is for the sake of his particular sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its last suggestion with the same פסוק. Money set aside for one sin may not be used for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though misused money loses its holiness and the offering would still atone, the פסוק sets the rule for how things should be done from the start. Both the animal and the money must be tied to the specific sin they were set aside for.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces a source from the תורה
For the sake of his specific sin

steps.whatToRemember: ׳קרבנו על חטאתו׳ means a חטאת, whether an animal or money, must be used only for the exact sin it was set aside for.

phrases.english: The verse states: "His offering for his sin" –

steps.title: What does ׳not misused and not atoned׳ mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא meant by saying the switched animal involves no מעילה and gives no atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean when it says ׳he did not misuse and it did not atone׳?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about an unclear phrase from earlier in the ברייתא about switching an animal. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase sounds strange. Why would the lack of מעילה have anything to do with whether the animal atones? The גמרא wants to know how these two parts connect.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not misuse, and it did not atone

phrases.english: What is [the meaning of] "he did not misuse and it did not atone"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to clarify a phrase from the ברייתא's earlier section on animals
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the ברייתא connects 'no מעילה' with 'no atonement' for a switched animal

steps.title: An animal can never be misused, so it can never be switched
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר שימי explains: since an animal for the מזבח can never lose its holiness through מעילה, it also cannot atone for a different sin, so it can never be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר שימי explained it in front of רב פפא. This is what it means: since one cannot misuse the animal, it also cannot atone for another sin. Because of that, he cannot switch it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר שימי explains that the two parts of the phrase depend on each other. Because the animal can never be made ordinary through misuse, it can never be moved over to a different sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, misuse removes the holiness, and then the money can work for something else. An animal for the מזבח keeps its holiness no matter what, so it stays stuck to its original sin. That is why it 'does not atone' for any other sin.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it
One cannot misuse it; its holiness cannot be removed
To switch or change it to another use

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Shimi explained it

phrases.english: it also cannot atone [for a different sin];

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No מעילה is possible with an animal, so it stays bound to its original sin and cannot atone for another.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא needed to teach the rule about money
steps.stepSummary: Money can be misused, and then it can work for another use. So one might have thought it may be switched from the start, and the ברייתא teaches that it may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But money is different. If he switches it, he has committed מעילה and brings a קרבן מעילה. So you might say he may use it for another sin from the start too. The ברייתא teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר שימי finishes his explanation by showing why the ברייתא needed a separate teaching for money. With money, someone might have thought switching is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a switch of money does work after the fact, through מעילה and a קרבן מעילה, one might conclude it is fine to do from the start. The ברייתא, through ׳קרבנו על חטאתו׳, says no. Working after the fact does not mean it is allowed from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought for misusing consecrated property
From the start, before acting
It teaches us (something we might have thought otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'it works after the fact' with 'it is allowed.' Switched money does end up atoning through מעילה, but you may not plan to switch it.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal can never be switched because its holiness never leaves it. Money can technically be switched through מעילה, but the פסוק forbids doing so from the start.

phrases.english: But money, since if he switches it
he has misused [it] and brings an offering for misuse –
one might say that from the outset too he may bring [an offering for another sin with it],
[therefore] it teaches us [that he may not].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מָעוֹת, כֵּיוָן דְּאִי מְשַׁנֵּי מָעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation by contrasting money with the animal
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule about money was needed because, unlike an animal, money can be misused and switched after the fact.

steps.title: New משנה: buying a different kind of offering with consecrated money
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists which offerings may be bought with money set aside for another kind: a lamb and a goat for each other, birds from either, and flour from birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may bring a female goat from money set aside for a female lamb, and a female lamb from money set aside for a female goat. From money set aside for a lamb or goat, one may bring turtledoves and young pigeons. From money set aside for birds, one may bring a tenth of an איפה of flour.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that money set aside for one type of חטאת may be used for a different type in certain cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb and a goat are the same level, so money for one may buy the other. The משנה also allows going down a level, from animals to birds and from birds to flour, as in the sliding-scale offering (קרבן עולה ויורד).

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property (here, money set aside for an offering)
A female lamb
A female goat
Turtledoves and young pigeons
A tenth of an איפה (a measure of fine flour)

steps.whyThisMatters: After the strict rule that a חטאת must match its own sin, this משנה shows that switching the type of animal or level of offering is sometimes allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One may bring a female goat from [money] consecrated for a female lamb,
[and] a female lamb from [money] consecrated for a female goat,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ כִּשְׂבָּה וּשְׂעִירָה – תּוֹרִין וּבְנֵי יוֹנָה,
phrases.english: and turtledoves and young pigeons from [money] consecrated for a female lamb and a female goat,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ תּוֹרִין וּבְנֵי יוֹנָה – עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה.
phrases.english: and a tenth of an ephah [of flour] from [money] consecrated for turtledoves and young pigeons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money set aside for a lamb or goat may buy the other, or birds. Money set aside for birds may buy a tenth of an איפה of flour.

steps.title: The משנה's example: becoming poorer or richer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives an example. Money set aside for a lamb or goat goes down to a bird, then to flour, if the owner becomes poor. Money set aside for flour goes up to a bird, then to a lamb or goat, if he becomes rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If someone set aside money for a female lamb or a female goat and then became poor, he brings a bird. If he became even poorer, he brings a tenth of an איפה of flour. If he set aside money for a tenth of an איפה and then became rich, he brings a bird. If he became even richer, he brings a female lamb or a female goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is giving a real-life example of the list it just gave. It shows how the money moves down or up between the levels of the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the קרבן עולה ויורד: a rich person brings an animal, a poorer person brings birds, and a very poor person brings flour. The משנה shows that money already set aside follows the owner's current wealth, in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: The sliding-scale sin offering, whose level depends on how rich the person is
He set aside (money for an offering)
A female lamb / a female goat, the top level of the offering
A tenth of an איפה of fine flour, the lowest level
He became poor / he became rich

phrases.english: How so?
If he set aside money for a female lamb or for a female goat,
and he became poor, he brings a bird;
if he became even poorer, he brings a tenth of an ephah of flour.
If he set aside money for a tenth of an ephah,
and he became rich, he brings a bird;
if he became even richer, he brings a female lamb or a female goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the משנה's list in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money set aside for one level of the קרבן עולה ויורד moves down or up to match the owner's new wealth.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where the משנה's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13 to 16 taught that money may not be moved to a different sin. So the גמרא needs a source that allows moving it between levels of the same offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just finished
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that allows switching money between levels of the offering

steps.title: Three extra phrases in the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא points out that the תורה says ״מחטאתו״ twice and ״על חטאתו״ once, and asks what these words come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: ״From his sin,״ ״from his sin,״ and ״over his sin.״ What do these words come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first points to three phrases, one written at each level of the offering, and asks why they are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is written at a different level: the lamb, the bird and the flour. The ברייתא says these words seem extra and must be teaching something. It gives the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From his sin.' Written at the lamb level and again at the bird level
'Over his sin.' Written at the flour level
What does the פסוק come to teach? (used when words seem extra)

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"From his sin," "from his sin,"
"Over his sin,"
what does the verse come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 19 by bringing a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is three extra phrases about 'his sin' in the פסוקים of the קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: The phrases allow switching between levels
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the phrases teach that money set aside for one kind of offering may be used for another kind: lamb and goat for each other, birds from either one, and flour from birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you learn that from money set aside for a lamb you may bring a goat, and from money for a goat a lamb? And from money set aside for a lamb or goat you may bring turtledoves or young pigeons? And from money set aside for turtledoves or young pigeons you may bring a tenth of an איפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra words are the source that allows money to move from one kind of offering to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording sounds like a question ('from where?'), but it really means: these words are the source for this switching. The list matches the משנה from step 17. All of it stays within the same sin, which fits step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you say...? (here it introduces what the extra words teach)
Something made holy. Here, money set aside for an offering
Turtledoves and young pigeons, the bird level of the offering

steps.confusionAlert: 'מנין' looks like a new question, but it is the ברייתא's answer to 'מה תלמוד לומר.' It tells us what the extra words come to teach.

phrases.english: From where do you say
that one may bring a goat from money consecrated for a lamb,
and a lamb from money consecrated for a goat,
and from money consecrated for a lamb or a goat
one may bring turtledoves or young pigeons,
and from money consecrated for turtledoves or young pigeons
one may bring a tenth of an ephah of flour?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שֶׁמְּבִיאִין מֵהֶקְדֵּשׁ כִּשְׂבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'מה תלמוד לומר' of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words allow money set aside for one kind of the offering to be used for another kind.

steps.title: The ברייתא's example, matching the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the same example as the משנה. A person who becomes poorer goes down a level, and a person who becomes richer goes up a level.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If he set aside money for a female lamb or a female goat and became poor, he brings a bird. If he became even poorer, he brings a tenth of an איפה. If he set aside money for a tenth of an איפה and became rich, he brings a bird. If he became even richer, he brings a female lamb or a female goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives an example, almost word for word like the משנה. This shows that the משנה's rule comes from this ברייתא and its פסוקים. The ברייתא continues with one more case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The example is the same as in step 18. Only small words are swapped: the ברייתא says 'lamb and goat' at the start and 'lamb or goat' at the end, the opposite of the משנה. The meaning is the same both times: one animal, either a lamb or a goat.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
'Or.' It shows the person brings just one of the two animals

steps.whatToRemember: The three phrases about 'his sin' in the פסוקים teach that money set aside for a קרבן עולה ויורד follows the owner's wealth, down or up. It still must be used for the same sin.

phrases.english: How so?
If he set aside money for a female lamb or a female goat and became poor,
he brings a bird;
if he became even poorer, he brings a tenth of an ephah;
if he set aside money for a tenth of an ephah and became rich,
he brings a bird;
if he became even richer, he brings a female lamb or a female goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the rule from step 21, matching the משנה in step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's rule comes from the ברייתא's reading of the extra words: money set aside moves down or up between levels to match the owner's wealth.

steps.title: A blemished lamb can become a bird, but a blemished bird cannot become flour
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The money from a blemished lamb or goat can buy a bird. A blemished bird cannot be exchanged for a flour offering, because a bird has no redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set aside a female lamb or goat and it became blemished, he may use its money to bring a bird. If he set aside a bird and it became blemished, he may not use its money to bring a tenth of an איפה of flour, because a bird cannot be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule. It covers what happens when the actual animal or bird that was set aside becomes unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal can be redeemed for money, and a poorer owner can use that money for a bird. A consecrated bird can never be redeemed at all. So a blemished bird never turns into money, and there is nothing to spend on flour. This is a special outcome caused by the bird's status. It does not limit the general rule that money set aside for a bird can go down to flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Became unfit (here, blemished) for the altar
With their money (the redemption money)
A tenth of an ephah of fine flour, the poorest person's offering
Redemption: exchanging something holy for money

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the end of the sugya. Here, the bird itself was set aside and it cannot be redeemed. Later, the גמרא talks about money set aside for a bird, and that money can go down to flour.

phrases.english: If he set aside a female lamb or goat and they became blemished –
he may bring a bird with their money,
phrases.notes: He redeems the blemished animal for money, and if he has become poorer he uses that money for a bird.

phrases.english: if he set aside a bird and it became blemished –
he may not bring a tenth of an ephah with its money,
because a bird has no redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 22 with the case of a blemished offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemished lamb or goat may be redeemed and its money used for a bird. A blemished bird cannot become flour, since birds cannot be redeemed.

steps.title: The verses behind the rules
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes by naming the פסוקים behind all these rules: ״מחטאתו״ and ״על חטאתו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the תורה says "from his sin" and "over his sin."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by pointing back to the words it started with. These are the source for everything it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opened in step 20 by asking what these phrases come to teach. It now closes the circle. ״מחטאתו״ appears by the lamb/goat and by the bird. ״על חטאתו״ appears by the flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, for this reason
"From his sin": the phrase written by the lamb/goat and by the bird
"Over his sin": the phrase written by the flour offering

steps.whatToRemember: ״מחטאתו״ is written twice (lamb/goat and bird) and ״על חטאתו״ once (flour). These words are the source for moving set-aside money between levels of the offering.

phrases.english: Therefore it is said
"from his sin," "over his sin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא by tying all its rules back to the פסוקים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The phrases ״מחטאתו״ and ״על חטאתו״ are the source for all the rules of moving set-aside money between levels.

steps.title: Both mentions of the phrase were needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that ״מחטאתו״ had to be written both by the lamb/goat and by the bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write "from his sin" by the female lamb or goat, and it was necessary to write it by the bird too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that both mentions of ״מחטאתו״ are needed. This line is setting up the next move, where it explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reader might think one mention would be enough to teach that set-aside money can move between levels. The גמרא claims that each mention teaches something the other could not. It will prove this in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
To write
Regarding, in the section about

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "from his sin"
regarding a female lamb or goat,
and it was necessary to write it regarding a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא names its sources, the גמרא explains why the same phrase appears twice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both mentions of ״מחטאתו″, by the lamb/goat and by the bird, are needed.

steps.title: What we would learn from the lamb alone
steps.stepSummary: Suppose ״מחטאתו״ were written only by the lamb/goat. We would learn that lamb money can go down to a bird, because both are blood offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse were written only about a consecrated lamb or goat, I would have said this: when someone set aside money for a lamb and became poor, he may transfer that money to a bird and bring a bird, because a lamb and a bird are both blood offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what the lamb/goat verse would teach if it stood alone. This sets up why a second verse is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lamb and bird are similar, since both are blood offerings. So moving money between them is easy to accept. This step limits what the first verse can teach: only a move between two blood offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an initial assumption that is later corrected)
Something made holy for the Temple
Becomes poor
He may transfer them (the money's holiness) onto
Kinds of blood offerings (animals and birds, whose blood goes on the altar)

phrases.english: For if the verse had written it
only regarding a consecrated female lamb or goat,
I would have said:
if he set aside [money for] a lamb,
when he becomes poor, that money
he may transfer onto a bird, so that he brings a bird,
because a lamb and a bird
are both kinds of blood offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּתִיב קְרָא גַּבֵּי הֶקְדֵּשׁ כִּשְׂבָּה אוֹ שְׂעִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the claim of step 25 by showing what the first verse alone would teach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lamb/goat verse alone would only allow moving money between two blood offerings (lamb to bird).

steps.title: Without the bird verse, bird money could not go to flour
steps.stepSummary: Flour is not a blood offering. Without the bird verse, we would think bird money cannot buy flour. The poor man would have to buy flour with his own money, and the bird money would go to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a tenth of an איפה is not a blood offering. If the פסוק had not written "from his sin" by the bird, I would have said this: when someone sets aside money for his pair of birds and becomes poorer, he does not bring flour with it, because flour is not a blood offering. Instead, he brings flour from his own house, and the money he set aside goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake we would make without the bird verse. This step sets up the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour is a different kind of offering from a bird. So the lamb-to-bird lesson would not carry over to bird-to-flour. We would still require the poor man to bring flour. However, we would make him pay for it separately and send the set-aside money to gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: His "nest": his pair of birds for the offering
He brings
From his house, meaning with his own other money
Gift offerings, brought voluntarily

phrases.english: But a tenth of an ephah
which is not a kind of blood offering,
if the verse had not written
"from his sin" regarding a bird,
I would have said:
when he sets aside money for his pair of birds and becomes poorer –
he does not bring a tenth of an ephah [with it],
because it is not a kind of blood offering,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַיְיתֵי עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה מִן בֵּיתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: rather, he brings a tenth of an ephah from his house,
and that money which he set aside
would go to gift offerings –

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה דְּלָאו מִינֵי דְּדָמִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 26: lamb to bird works logically, but bird to flour would not.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the bird verse, bird money could not buy flour. He would pay for flour separately, and the bird money would go to gift offerings.

steps.title: The second verse allows bird money to buy flour
steps.stepSummary: That is why the תורה repeats ״מחטאתו״ by the bird. It teaches that money set aside for a bird may also be used to bring the flour offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק writes "from his sin" again by the bird: to teach that he may also bring a tenth of an איפה from money consecrated for a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes its explanation. The second ״מחטאתו״ is needed so that bird money can go down to flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mention covers moving money between blood offerings. The second mention teaches something new: money can even move from a blood offering to a flour offering. So each mention has its own job, and neither is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason, therefore
It is written again
To say, to teach
Also

steps.whatToRemember: ״מחטאתו״ by the lamb teaches that money can move between blood offerings (lamb to bird). ״מחטאתו״ by the bird teaches that money can move even to flour, which is not a blood offering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of a צריכותא: the גמרא shows that a repeated phrase is not extra, because each mention teaches its own lesson.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse writes again
"from his sin" regarding a bird,
to say that from consecrated money of a bird
he may also bring a tenth of an ephah,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the mistaken assumption of step 27 by showing the second verse corrects it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The repeated ״מחטאתו״ by the bird teaches that money set aside for a bird offering may be used for the flour offering when the owner becomes poorer.

steps.title: What ״על חטאתו״ by the flour offering teaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ״על חטאתו״ by the עשירית האיפה means: money set aside for flour can be added to and used for a bird, or for a lamb or goat, if the person became richer.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק is saying: if someone set aside money for a tenth of an איפה of flour, and before he brought it he became richer, he adds to that money and brings a bird. If he became richer still, he adds to it and brings a female lamb or goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second פסוק, ״על חטאתו״, which is written by the flour offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 25-28 showed that ״מחטאתו״ lets money go DOWN to a cheaper offering. Here ״על חטאתו״ teaches the opposite direction: flour money can go UP. The person keeps using the same coins and simply adds more.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה of fine flour, the offering of the very poor
"Over his sin", the פסוק written by the flour offering
He became richer
He adds money to the coins he already set aside

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק ״על חטאתו״ written by the flour offering (ויקרא 5:13).

phrases.english: When he sets aside money for a tenth of an ephah of flour,
and before he brought it, he became richer,
he adds to the coins and brings a bird;
if he became richer still, he adds to them
and brings a female lamb or a female goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing ״מחטאתו״ in step 28, the גמרא turns to the second פסוק named in the ברייתא, ״על חטאתו״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money set aside for the flour offering may be added to and used to buy a bird or a lamb/goat if the owner becomes richer.

steps.title: Why write ״על חטאתו״ by the flour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ״על חטאתו״ had to be written specifically by the flour offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is ״על חטאתו״ written by the tenth of an איפה of flour?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next move: why put this פסוק by the flour, and not only by the bird?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the question about ״מחטאתו״ in step 25. The גמרא wants to show that the פסוק is not extra, and that the flour case needed its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason?
By, in connection with

phrases.english: And what is the reason that "over his sin" is written
by the tenth of an ephah of flour?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the פסוק explained in step 29 was placed by the flour offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the upgrade rule needed to be written by the flour offering in particular.

steps.title: If written only by the bird, we would limit it to blood offerings
steps.stepSummary: If ״על חטאתו״ were written only by the bird, we would think only bird money can be upgraded to a lamb or goat, because both are blood offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ״על חטאתו״ were written by the bird, I would have said: only when someone set aside money for his pair of birds and became richer does he add to it and bring a lamb or goat, since both are kinds of blood offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by showing what mistake we would make if the פסוק were written only by the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird and a lamb are both offerings whose blood is placed on the מזבח, so moving money between them seems natural. That similarity would make us think the upgrade rule works only between blood offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
His pair of birds
Types of blood offerings

phrases.english: For if "over his sin" were written by the bird,
I would have said:
when he sets aside money for his pair of birds and becomes richer,
that is when he adds to the coins
and brings a female lamb or a female goat,
since both of them are kinds of blood offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּתַיב ״עַל חַטָּאתוֹ״ גַּבֵּי עוֹף, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bird money could be upgraded to an animal because both are blood offerings, so a bird פסוק alone would not cover flour.

steps.title: Without the flour verse, flour money could not be upgraded
steps.stepSummary: Without the פסוק by the flour, we would think flour money cannot be added to. The richer man would buy a bird or animal with new money, and the flour money would go to gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he set aside money for flour and became richer, we would say about the money he set aside: if he did not become much richer, he brings a bird; if he became much richer, he brings a lamb or goat; and the money he set aside goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by describing the mistaken rule we would have had for the flour money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour has no blood, so it seems too different from a bird or animal to share money with them. We would have thought he must buy the new offering with fresh money, and the old flour money would be used for gift offerings. This is the same idea as step 27, but now going upward.

keyTerms.meaning: Very much
The money goes to gift offerings

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה וְהֶעֱשִׁיר,
phrases.english: But if he set aside money for a tenth of an ephah of flour and became richer,
as for those coins he set aside,
phrases.notes: He means we would think he cannot add to these coins. He would buy the new offering with other money.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא הֶעֱשִׁיר טוּבָא – נַיְיתֵי עוֹף,
phrases.english: if he did not become much richer, he brings a bird,
and if he became much richer,
he brings a female lamb or a female goat,
and those coins that he set aside
go to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה וְהֶעֱשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 31 by stating what we would wrongly conclude about flour money.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because flour is not a blood offering, we would have said flour money cannot be upgraded and must go to gift offerings.

steps.title: That is why both verses are written
steps.stepSummary: The תורה writes ״מחטאתו״ by the rich and poor offerings and ״על חטאתו״ by the very poor offering, so we can learn everything explained above.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק writes ״מחטאתו״ by the sin offering of wealth and poverty, and ״על חטאתו״ by the offering of extreme poverty: to learn them as we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the explanation of both פסוקים from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מחטאתו״, by the lamb and the bird, lets money move down to a cheaper offering. ״על חטאתו״, by the flour, lets money move up to a more expensive one. Together they show that in every case the same set-aside money is used, never sent to gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason
Extreme poverty, the level of the flour offering
To expound, to learn from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: ״מחטאתו״ (by the lamb and the bird) teaches that set-aside money can go down to a cheaper offering. ״על חטאתו״ (by the flour) teaches that it can go up to a more expensive one. Both are needed because flour is not a blood offering.

phrases.english: That is why the verse writes
by this sin offering of wealth and poverty
"from his sin",
and by extreme poverty, "over his sin",
to expound as we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the explanation of why both פסוקים are needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both ״מחטאתו״ and ״על חטאתו״ are needed, so that set-aside money moves both down and up between the levels of קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: A rich person who defiled the מקדש and set aside birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, begins a new case: a rich person who became טמא in the מקדש and set aside a pair of birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: a rich person who defiled the מקדש and set aside a pair of birds...
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins here. The גמרא is setting up a case whose ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rich person who entered the מקדש while טמא must bring a lamb or goat, not birds. So setting aside a pair of birds was the wrong offering for him, and the ruling about what happens to them is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who entered the מקדש or ate holy food while טמא
A pair of birds set aside as an offering
A rich person

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
A rich person who defiled the Temple
who set aside a pair of birds

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא's explanation is finished, a new אמורא statement opens a related case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is being set up (a rich מטמא מקדש who set aside birds). The ruling continues on the next amud.
